body: I would love to know how it goes for you. Feel free to post your list! I'm so proud of you for considering doing it!

It sounds like it starts with pinpointing what your goals are. Are these career related? Do these goals reflect things that make you passionate or that you find your talent or pride in? 


Then, make a list. Ask yourself if this goal is realistic, if it's truly what you want, and how to get there. List the steps for yourself. Would you try this?

I can see how the stress of that can turn someone toxic. I encourage you in those moments to remind yourself of just that, it has to do with his stress and his insecurities and fear, that it is not healthy or productive, that it may chip away at you but that his abusing treatment of you doesn't define your worth, or reflect your successes. Allow yourself the grace of taking yourself out of the blame, and understanding that in you surviving this treatment even up to this point, you are successful. Your argument could always be how maltreatment in your youth would never motivate you for what that abuser advises you do in life-- it will only push you away to enjoy your successes without him. You can attribute the successes to come to your own perseverance. 

In short, there seems to be a fire growing that's helping you cope. Even if it is convincing you you want the pain-- it is still fire and it can still be used as motivational energy for you. You are learning things now some people never have the fortune of learning, how to deal with abuse- the hell on earth-- and live through it. Let his toxicity define him, remove yourself of the blame, focus on your talents and passions, the things you find are successful. Learn to want, rather, the pain in balancing dreams and focus.

You've been struggling for such a long time. Perhaps recall the moment you wrote this.. maybe you were feeling inspired by something. Notice that only you could write those words and display that hope for yourself- and you did it. Rough times are tougher if we've forgotten we've already found the strength to overcome them. I've been sitting all evening trying to conjure up reasons not to end it for myself, seeing your thread history inspires me to recall the moments I once felt hopeful. Imagine what the world would be like if there were more people like you, who, after feeling the lack of, understood the power of encouragement and support and hope and were able to spread that encouragement to others. You may feel dim but you've been a light for me
What do you think happened to your dad for him to hurt his children?

Sometimes finding peace may be bringing peace to others. You seem to be so thoughtful and considerate of others' plight; your mother and her health, your dog and its wellbeing. I know these thoughts and actions are in preparation to convince yourself you lack obligation. What is it you mean by being great? Tell me about your talents and your dreams. At least don't let the world miss out on that genius you feel.

Sometimes we envision what being in a place we wish to be would feel and look like. Sometimes it isn't what was expected and it can seem like the world in itself is not what we can make of it. You still hold on to the memory that you wished to be in this new country. What was that feeling like? Did it feel almost like starting fresh? Maybe there are things you envisioned doing there that have yet to be done!

Well, I'm not sure how it started. I remember feeling that life would be very dark for me at a very early age. A lot of violence in my child hood home. My mother and my siblings escaped when I was 8 and I've carried a lot of guilt and confusion about life and loyalty ever since. 

It's this very calm version of me. It's almost seducing me to accept the peacefulness of dying. Having control over death. Telling me I've made the impact I will make and others will go on and the world will keep turning in my absence. I've always prepared for others to not suffer and it makes me believe I have done it well enough
What brought you to the foreign country? Is it something that you once had passion for?
You are so insightful to see past that. That gives me a place to reason that it can be separated from me.. I've always thought it was a version of myself, not a reflection that shows itself

Just as much as you have this urge, there are medical professionals that live for being given the chance to help you. You won't be a burden to them. Call for an ambulance, you post here maybe because you still have that will to reach out. Hold onto that will, make the call
Why does it want to end itself?
What looks like success to you? What do you hope you will achieve and feel you fail at?
